01

Setting specification

Task

Minimize $f$ globally over $B_2(0,R)$ and return a point with small objective gap.

Admissible model

$f:B_2(0,R)\to\mathbb{R}$ is convex and satisfies $|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\|x-y\|_2$ for every $x,y$ in the ball. Neither a definition nor regularity outside the ball is assumed. Continuity on the ball guarantees attainment of the constrained minimum.

Oracle interface

At any finite query point $x$ in $B_2(0,R)$, the oracle returns the single exact scalar $f(x)$. The reply is uniquely determined and contains no gradient, subgradient or derivative-vector product.

Projection and the stated proximal operations over known geometry are free.

The public inputs are $d$, $L$, $R$, $\varepsilon$, together with the sets, kernels and auxiliary operations explicitly declared above. Information about the unknown objective and any undisclosed sample distribution is obtained only through the stated interface.

Output

Return $\widehat{x}\in B_2(0,R)$. The output may be an unqueried point, an average or convex combination that remains in the stated space. No function value, gradient, inner solution, or accuracy certificate must accompany the output.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The base loss is $\ell(I,x)=f(x)-f_*$, where $f_*=\inf_{u\in B_2(0,R)}f(u)$. This nonnegative loss is evaluated at the output, with tolerance $\varepsilon$.

Resource accounting

Each scalar function value or noisy observation costs $1$ call. Every location in a multipoint finite difference, every initialization query, and every reference observation is charged.

Only the declared oracle resource is charged. Computation and storage using existing information, together with explicitly known geometric and proximal operations, are free.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Deterministic

Only deterministic strategies are allowed. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The requirement $\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon$ holds deterministically for each instance.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: $N\le T$ on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

Randomized

Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the instance and external randomness. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The error requirement is $\Pr(\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon)\ge2/3$.

Probability is over the algorithm's random seed only.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: $N\le T$ on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

Output qualification. Random selection among previously queried points is permitted, subject to the declared success guarantee.

Lower Bounds For Gradient-Free Convex Optimization And Convex-Concave Saddle-Point Problems ↗Local argument in this profile · see complete PDF / LaTeX ↗
Conditions
$d\ge d_0,\ A\ge C,\ A^2>d,\ A\ge64$; $L,R>0$ and $A=LR/\varepsilon$.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Oracle correspondence
Restrict globally beta_h-smooth source objectives to the ball with beta_h=L/(2R), R_h=R. They are L-Lipschitz there. One target exact scalar value is one unrestricted source value; no derivatives or outside-ball capability is added to the target.
Guarantee conversion
Any uniformly correct deterministic target algorithm is a seed-independent source algorithm with success probability one, so the randomized source lower bound applies.
Output rule
The source global minimizer is feasible, so constrained and global minima coincide. Any feasible target output, including an unqueried point, is permitted by the source.
Resource conversion
Identical fixed worst-case scalar-value cap on every execution path. The exact transferred inequality is T>=max{5d/16,(d/4096)min{d,sqrt(A/2)}} for A>=64.
Branch condition
$A\ge64$ within this existing $d\ge d_0,\ A\ge C,\ A^2>d$ comparison.
Upper bound
\[O(\min\{dA^2\log(edA),d^2\log(ed)\log(4A)\})\]

/proofs/0/body · SHA-256 5302a8df00b684fda4ba426691ee465e9cb0c9988936fa01b2026ed2eb070a28
A deterministic procedure obtains an $\eta$-accurate subgradient at a point within distance $\zeta$ of the requested point using at most $7d\lceil\log_2(2L\sqrt d/\eta)\rceil$ values. It yields the convex upper $O(dA^2\log(edA))$ and the strongly convex upper $O(dL^2\log(edA)/(\mu\varepsilon))$, with $A=LR/\varepsilon$. For a convex one-dimensional restriction, maintain an active interval whose every subderivative lies in $[\ell,u]$. Divide it into six equal pieces and query its seven grid points. Their secant slopes satisfy $s_0\le\cdots\le s_5$. The intervals $[q_1,q_2]$ and $[q_4,q_5]$ have protected subgradient envelopes $[s_0,s_2]$ and $[s_3,s_5]$. Since $(s_2-s_0)+(s_5-s_3)\le u-\ell$, selecting the narrower one halves the envelope width and divides the interval length by six. Set $\tau=\eta/\sqrt d$, $k=\lceil\log_2(2L/\tau)\rceil$, and $r_1=\zeta/2$. At coordinate $j$, run $k$ subdivisions from half-width $r_j$, move to the final midpoint, and retain the two protected secants of denominator $h_j=2r_j6^{-k}$. Set $r_{j+1}=\tau h_j/(16L)$. Then $r_{j+1}/r_j\le1/8$, and all later displacement is at most $\tau h_j/(8L)$. Translating a protected secant by this displacement changes its slope by at most $\tau/4$. Thus every subgradient of the final common point $y$ has coordinate $j$ in $[\ell_j-\tau/4,u_j+\tau/4]$. The midpoint vector differs from every such subgradient by at most $3\eta/4$ in Euclidean norm. All probe and protection points lie within $\zeta$ of the original point. The scales may be very small, but are positive and require the same finite number of queries. For a globally Lipschitz convex function and a public projected set $K\subseteq B_2(R)$ containing zero, the extracted vector satisfies $$f(z)\ge f(x)+\langle\widehat g,z-x\rangle-2L\zeta-2R\eta\quad(z\in K).$$ Choose $\zeta=\varepsilon/(16L)$, $\eta=\varepsilon/(16R)$, so the model error is $\varepsilon/4$ and $\|\widehat g\|\le2L$ in the stated nontrivial range. Projected subgradient descent with step $R/(2L\sqrt N)$ gives averaged gap at most $2LR/\sqrt N+\varepsilon/4$. Taking $N\ge64A^2$ proves the convex rate. The probes may leave $K$ only in the all-space variant. For a function defined on the ball, keep iterates in $B_2(R-2\delta)$. For strong convexity, apply extraction to $h(x)=f(x)-\mu\|x\|^2/2$, which is convex and at most $2L$-Lipschitz because $\mu R\le L$. Choose $\delta=\gamma/(16L)$, vector error $\eta=\gamma/(8R)$, and add $\mu x$ back. Then $\|\widehat g\|\le4L$ and $$f(z)\ge f(x)+\langle\widehat g,z-x\rangle+\mu\|z-x\|^2/2-\gamma.$$ With $a_t=2/[\mu(t+1)]$, projection, and $D_t=\|x_t-x_*\|^2$, $$f(x_t)-f(x_*)-\gamma\le\frac{\mu(t-1)}4D_t-\frac{\mu(t+1)}4D_{t+1}+\frac{16L^2}{\mu(t+1)}.$$ Multiply by $t$ and sum. The initial distance coefficient is zero, and the remaining distance terms telescope. The weighted average has gap at most $32L^2/[\mu(T+1)]+\gamma$. Taking $\gamma=\varepsilon/8$ and $T+1\ge128L^2/(\mu\varepsilon)$, including shrinkage loss at most $2L\delta$, proves the result. Ordinary convex projected descent gives the $A^2$ branch. Deterministic value localization supplies the separate $d^2\log(ed)\log(4A)$ branch; take the minimum only among applicable branches. For a known body $B_2(r_{\rm in})\subseteq K\subseteq B_2(R_{\rm out})$, the identity $(1-a)K+aB_2(r_{\rm in})\subseteq K$ supplies feasible probe room. Choose $a=\gamma/(16LR_{\rm out})$ and probe radius at most $ar_{\rm in}/2$. Shrinkage costs at most $LaR_{\rm out}$. The query count is independent of the probe radius and uses $R_{\rm out}$ in place of $R$. A finite-sum mean value costs $n$ component values, multiplying these deterministic bounds by $n$.

/proofs/1/body · SHA-256 22a37def08b7d321ee101fa614c49bf15f038bb3f82579c82fc250f797c52cb7
For the smooth class, $Q\ge128^2$ gives $\Omega(d\log Q)$. This also holds in a public strongly convex class with $\kappa\ge2$. For a ball-restricted Lipschitz class, $A=LR/\varepsilon\ge6\cdot128^2$ gives $\Omega(d\log A)$. Dorn et al., Theorem 2.5, gives $$\frac{3d}{4000}\left[1+\frac{\log(\beta_hR_h^2/\varepsilon)}{\log((\beta_h+\mu_h)/(\beta_h-\mu_h))}\right]$$ when $\mu_h/\beta_h\in[1/2,1]$ and $\beta_hR_h^2/\varepsilon\ge128^2$. Choose $\mu_h=\beta_h/2$, so the denominator is $\log3$. A convex $\beta$-smooth class contains this subclass with $\beta_h=\beta$, $R_h=R$. A public lower curvature budget $\mu\le\beta/2$ also contains it, uniformly in the public condition number. For the ball-restricted Lipschitz class choose $R_h=R/2$, $\beta_h=2L/(3R)$, and $\mu_h=\beta_h/2$. On $B_2(R)$, $\|\nabla f(x)\|\le\beta_h(\|x\|+\|x_*\|)\le L$, and the global minimizer remains inside the feasible ball. One source value simulates one restricted value. The stronger source oracle permits all such algorithms, and $Q_h=A/6$. The explicit window makes $\log(A/6)$ and $\log A$ uniformly comparable. For a selected-component finite sum with all components equal to the same hard function, one component query is one source query. This transfer has cost one, not $n$. A logarithmic and a dimension-dependent lower bound may be maximized only where both respective windows hold.

/proofs/2/body · SHA-256 e337fe1bbdc7a8471c27bff8578ac9695fda39f5bd738324501658aee12cbc83
A public feasible point whose objective gap is at most $G_0$ solves every target $\varepsilon\ge G_0$ with exactly zero calls. For a convex mean objective that is $L$-Lipschitz on a ball of radius $R$, the center has gap at most $LR$. A sample Lipschitz modulus $G$ with $\mathbb E G^r\le L^r$, $r>1$, implies $\mathbb E G\le L$, so the same certificate applies to moment models. Integrability at one point ensures that the mean is defined. If a globally $\beta$-smooth objective has a global minimizer within distance $R$ of the public initial point, its gradient vanishes at that minimizer and the smoothness inequality gives gap at most $\beta R^2/2$. In a declared norm, use the corresponding radius in that norm. For $B_p(R)$ with Euclidean regularity this radius is $R$ when $p\le2$ and $R d^{1/2-1/p}$ when $p\ge2$. For a known positive semidefinite quadratic matrix $A$, the center has gap at most $\lambda_{\max}(A)R^2/2$; if $A=0$, the loss is identically zero. A public initial-gap promise $\Delta$ directly gives the certificate $G_0=\Delta$. For the Markov potential $r_0$, its companion initial iterate has gap at most $\mu r_0$. These are different certificates with different model assumptions; in particular, an unknown matrix with no public spectral bound does not acquire a uniform certificate. Call counts are nonnegative. Together with the stated algorithm, this proves exact zero complexity on each certified region. The upper/lower ratio is undefined, so it is stored as null rather than as $0/0$.

/proofs/3/body · SHA-256 9b9e47c8f3586db0e12f7b72f3856642903a5c8f5be7be5a7f6d54eb259851ec
Write A=LR/epsilon>1. Upper bound: start with [a,b]=[-R,R]. Query u=a+(b-a)/3 and v=b-(b-a)/3, charging both exact scalar values. If f(u)<=f(v), retain [a,v]; otherwise retain [u,b]. Convexity ensures that the retained closed interval contains a constrained minimizer, including in the equality case. After k steps its length is 2R(2/3)^k. Its midpoint is feasible and is within R(2/3)^k of a retained minimizer, so its objective gap is at most LR(2/3)^k. Taking k=ceil(log(A)/log(3/2)) gives a deterministic budget of 2k values and requires no value at the output. The finite comparisons and affine updates are Borel. This proves O(log(4A)) deterministically and hence also for the randomized 2/3 guarantee. Lower bound for every A>1: f_+(x)=Lx and f_-(x)=-Lx are admissible on [-R,R]. Their epsilon-success sets satisfy x<=-R+epsilon/L and x>=R-epsilon/L respectively, and are disjoint when epsilon<LR. A zero-query output distribution is common to both objectives; its two success probabilities sum to at most one. Thus the randomized 2/3 guarantee, and also the deterministic guarantee, require at least one scalar-value query. Logarithmic lower bound: use the subclass transfer in accepted local proof ZO_PROOF_PRECISION_LOG, with its primary premise independently reread here. Dorn et al., arXiv:2610.00345v1, source SHA256 1869dd758da361249e15ca5c9bc20792f55d6d7432b04be0d818323539baf105, Section 2 characters 6700-11900, Theorem 2.5 characters 13496-15396, and Theorem E.5/Section E.4 characters 112800-119800, uses a fixed worst-case budget and pointwise success probability 2/3 for arbitrary adaptive randomized exact-value algorithms. Its queries and outputs are unrestricted. The dimension-times-depth lower argument applies for d=1 as well. Set source localization radius R_h=R/2, smoothness beta_h=2L/(3R), and strong convexity mu_h=beta_h/2. Every source function has a global minimizer x_* in [-R/2,R/2]. Since its gradient vanishes there, for |x|<=R we have |f'(x)|<=beta_h(|x|+|x_*|)<=L. Restriction to [-R,R] is therefore an admissible target function, and its constrained minimum equals its global minimum. A target algorithm can be simulated with one source value per target value, and its feasible output is permitted by the stronger source model. The source ratio beta_h R_h^2/epsilon equals A/6. Theorem 2.5 consequently gives T>=(3/4000)[1+log(A/6)/log(3)] when A>=A_0=6*128^2=98304. This lower bound includes deterministic algorithms. Uniform combination: for A>=A_0, log(A/6)>=log(4A)/2, since A_0>=144. For 1<A<A_0, T>=1>=log(4A)/log(4A_0). Thus throughout A>1, T>=c log(4A), with c=min{1/log(4A_0),3/(8000 log(3))}>0. Together with the ternary-search upper bound this proves Theta(log(4A)) for both quantities. At A=1 the existing zero-query comparison applies; the new region is strict and does not include that endpoint. Any overlap with an existing high-accuracy comparison specializes to compatible bounds, while its higher-dimensional claims are untouched.

body
/proofs/4/body · SHA-256 94bd02d6fa37eb9fb0a9abf677a153d3767b20e4b9e976ff5d770466736ddf08
Primary premise: Dorn et al., arXiv:2610.00345v1, Section 2 and Theorem 2.1, archived SHA256 1869dd758da361249e15ca5c9bc20792f55d6d7432b04be0d818323539baf105, source characters 8930-11780 (theorem begins at 10190). For globally beta_h-smooth convex objectives with a global minimizer in B_2(0,R_h), fixed-budget adaptive randomized exact-value algorithms with per-objective success at least 2/3 require T>=max{5d/16,(d/4096)min{d,sqrt(beta_h R_h^2/epsilon)}} when epsilon<=beta_h R_h^2/32. Queries and outputs may be unrestricted. Set R_h=R and beta_h=L/(2R). For every source objective choose a global minimizer x_* with norm at most R. Its gradient vanishes. On B_2(0,R), ||grad f(x)||_2<=beta_h ||x-x_*||_2<=2 beta_h R=L. Integrating along segments in the ball proves that the restriction is convex and L-Lipschitz. Its constrained minimum equals the source global minimum. A target algorithm on this restricted objective is simulated using exactly one source scalar evaluation for each target value. The ball-restricted queries and feasible, possibly unqueried output are allowed by the stronger source model. The output gap and private-seed success probability are unchanged, and the same fixed worst-case cap holds on every path. Thus a uniformly successful target randomized algorithm would solve every source instance. Deterministic algorithms are included as seed-independent algorithms. Here beta_h R_h^2/epsilon=A/2, so the theorem window is exactly A>=64 and gives T>=max{5d/16,(d/4096)min{d,sqrt(A/2)}}. Since min{d,sqrt(A/2)}>=min{d,sqrt(A)}/sqrt(2), this proves Omega(d min{d,sqrt(A)}) with universal constants. No new target smoothness or global-minimizer promise is imposed: these are properties only of an adversarial subclass. On each existing R2 domain d>=d_0, A>=C, A^2>d, retain the accepted lower Omega(d^2/log(ed)); retain the independent accepted Omega(d log A) only when A>=98304; add this new lower only when A>=64. Their maximum gives the displayed three-branch lower envelope. Below 64 the old envelope remains unchanged, and equality at 64 is included by the source theorem. At A=d^2 and d tending to infinity the new lower is Omega(d^2), while the stronger old term is Omega(d^2/log(ed)); the improvement is material. Upper bounds and logarithmic-gap labels remain valid; the gap expressions are recomputed as their upper envelope divided by the new compatible lower maximum. For A^2<=d and A>=64, the new d sqrt(A) rate is dominated by the accepted d A^2/log(e A^2) rate; no R1 change is needed. The zero-query region epsilon>=LR is disjoint from A>=64. At d=1 the transferred constant lower is dominated by the accepted Omega(log(4A)) one-dimensional envelope. Old lower-bound proofs and literature are retained conditionally, rather than recertified.

partition_argument
/joint_analysis/domain_map/partition_argument · SHA-256 718803b94b4fb410ba421cd3193fac62cb3cce2894bdff2048717cdfc3b14c8f
Split A<=1 from A>1, then d=1 from d>=2. On d>=2,A>1, R1 and R2 are disjoint by A^2<=d versus A^2>d; their logical complement is the residual cell. Thus every target pair is accounted for, including explicitly unassessed parameters. Source-guard intersections remain necessary within recorded cells; comparison labels do not certify broader applicability.

For each existing q1 quantity and its own view/guarantee, minimize the fixed worst-case number of exact scalar values over arbitrary adaptive algorithms. Deterministic correctness and randomized pointwise private-seed success >=2/3 remain separate. Domain: integer d>=1, L,R,epsilon>0, equivalently d>=1 and A>0. Queries and output lie in B_2(0,R); no regularity outside it is assumed. The invertible scaling h(y)=f(Ry)/(LR) gives unit radius, unit Lipschitz modulus and tolerance 1/A with one scalar call per query and unchanged guarantees. Thus d and A vary jointly without hiding dimension or precision in constants. Proof thresholds are universal fixed constants. Distinct q2 identities are outside adoption. All retained asymptotic envelopes below retain their native applicability and claim guards.

full_domain
/joint_analysis/target/full_domain · SHA-256 c1bc8ce079ce281ff9852dd72f30cfc5628caf907ff83723297ed87304f41a18
For each existing q1 quantity and its own view/guarantee, minimize the fixed worst-case number of exact scalar values over arbitrary adaptive algorithms. Deterministic correctness and randomized pointwise private-seed success >=2/3 remain separate. Domain: integer d>=1, L,R,epsilon>0, equivalently d>=1 and A>0. Queries and output lie in B_2(0,R); no regularity outside it is assumed. The invertible scaling h(y)=f(Ry)/(LR) gives unit radius, unit Lipschitz modulus and tolerance 1/A with one scalar call per query and unchanged guarantees. Thus d and A vary jointly without hiding dimension or precision in constants. Proof thresholds are universal fixed constants. Distinct q2 identities are outside adoption. All retained asymptotic envelopes below retain their native applicability and claim guards.
